answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A marble delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A violet check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A ocean penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 2696 identities need 2696 bonds of 41 tokens, 31803 dollars of hardware and 40 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
